Understand one thing, in both the scenarios Mr.Surve is making money. Which exactly happened in my case.
Be mindful when dealing with such brokers, Thank You.

My honest take on the India Budget 2026 (from a real estate lens)
This year’s Budget didn’t try to excite real estate.

And honestly, that might be its biggest message.
There were no dramatic sops.
No loud incentives.
No overnight “game changers”.

What it did signal instead was continuity.

A steady push on infrastructure.
Patience on housing policy.
And an acceptance that real estate doesn’t need adrenaline, it needs stability.

As someone who’s seen multiple cycles, I’ve learnt this the hard way:
Real estate grows best when the government doesn’t interfere too much.

Roads, metros, airports, logistics corridors, these matter far more than temporary tax tweaks.
They quietly change behaviour.
And behaviour is what moves markets.

What stood out for me:
• Continued infrastructure-led growth
• No sudden shocks to homebuyers or developers
• A clear focus on long-term capital formation

What didn’t happen is equally important.
No policy panic.
No artificial demand creation.

They regret the one they bought for the wrong reasons.

Or year two.
The regret shows up later.

When:

The home isn’t bad.
The decision just wasn’t honest.

Most buying mistakes don’t happen because of money.
They happen because of pressure.

• upgrade fast
